WIBAUX SERIES
The Wibaux series consists of shallow, undulating to very steep, excessively drained soils on dissected sedimentary uplands. Slopes range from 4 to 90 percent. They farmed in materials weathered in place from red, burned shale and porcelanite at elevations of 3400 to 4100 feet.
The vegetation is mainly bluebunch wheatgrass, needle-and-thread, fringed sagewort, broom snakeweed, and rubber rabbitbrush. Annual precipitation is 11 to 13 inches, mean annual soil temperature is 49 to 52 degrees F., the frost free season is 110 to 120 days.
Typically, the surface layer is reddish brown channery loam about 2 inches thick. The underlying material is reddish brown very channery loam resting on hard, red shale and sandstone at about 9 inches.
Permeability is moderately rapid, the effective rooting depth is about 10 inches. Available water holding capacity is 1 to 2 inches.
These soils are used for range.
A typical profile of Wibaux channery loam, grassland, 325 feet north and 265 feet west of the S 1/16 corner of Sec. 21 and 22, T. 7 S., R. 40 E.
A 0 to 2 inches, reddish brown (2.5YR 5/4) channery loam, dark reddish brown (2.5YR 3/4) moist; weak, thin platy structure, soft, friable, nonsticky and slightly plastic; 25 percent of volume is thin, hard shale channer; clear smooth boundary. (1 to 4 inches thick)
2 to 5 inches, reddish brown (2.5YR 4/4) channery loam, dark reddish brown (2.5YR 3/4) moist; weak, medium blocky structure; slightly hard, friable, slightly sticky and slightly plastic; 25 percent of volume is shale channers; clear wavy boundary.
5 to 9 inches, reddish brown (2.5YR 5/4) very channery loam, reddish brown (2.5YR 4/4) moist; massive slightly hard, friable, slightly sticky and slightly plastic; 65 percent of volume is hard shale channers; slightly effervescent; abrupt irregular boundary.
R 9 to 12 inches, fractured, hard, red shale and sandstone.
